note: Sound rendering of a dense apauruṣeya/intention-to-speak argument; some commentary lines are set as verse and the opening 'dbang du ma byas pa' is paraphrased, but the argument is reproduced correctly.

errors.english: Some belong to my family [note: the Tathagata family]
errors.why: The speaker of this passage is Vajrapāṇi (the next side has 'ང་ནི་རྡོ་རྗེ་རིགས་ཞེས་རབ་ཏུ་བསྟན'), so 'my family' is the Vajra family, not the Tathāgata family.

fix.replace: [note: the Vajra family; the speaker is Vajrapāṇi]

errors.english: To subdue the secretive ones [note: likely referring to certain classes of spirits or obstacles]
errors.why: gsang ba pa is the proper class name Guhyaka (the yakṣa retinue of Vajrapāṇi), not a description 'secretive ones'.

note: Accurate account of the mantra counts by family, but the closing note misidentifies whose family 'my family' is.

errors.english: including the dental and cerebral letters
errors.why: The Tibetan names the added letters da dha ḍa ḍha ya la; the English drops ya and la and reduces the specific list to a category.

note: Faithful sādhana translation of the Vairocana visualization; only the list of added letters for the eighty minor marks is blurred.

errors.why: ltung byed is pātayantika (Mūlasarvāstivāda; Pali pācittiya); 'pāpayattika' is not an attested form.

errors.english: who shares the same symbols and views
errors.why: mtshan here is the sex/gender marks (liṅga): the struck monk must be of the same sex and views, not share 'symbols'.

note: Careful, complete rendering of the striking offence and its weapon lists; one garbled Sanskrit term and mtshan misread.

errors.english: they should remain simply by looking at the food; thus it is for both the work and the acquisitions.
errors.why: zan la bltas pa means relying on food alone; the Buddha says those who do not do the assigned work live on food only, with neither duty nor share of gains, not 'by looking at the food'.

note: Generally correct on duties, food shares and the no-offence cases; the quoted ruling on those who decline work is rendered too literally to make sense.
Accurate word-commentary on pātayantikas 27-29 and the lower-garment story; some boat terms are uncertain but defensibly rendered.

errors.english: and sent him off, though she was agitated by the haste of his departure
errors.why: It is the prince who, sent off by his mother, is flustered with haste (Skt. sa visṛṣṭas tvarākulaḥ), not the mother.

fix.find: and sent him off, though she was agitated by the haste of his departure
fix.replace: and sent him off, and he set out flustered with haste

errors.english: escaping in secret after he was ordered to be killed
errors.why: The minister says only 'surely this is the prince fleeing in secret' (Skt. gūḍhaṃ palāyate; gsad is a corruption of gsang); 'after he was ordered to be killed' is not in the text.

fix.find: escaping in secret after he was ordered to be killed

note: Narrative is followed correctly, but the subject of 'agitated by haste' is shifted to the mother and the minister's words carry an added clause.

errors.english: By merely purifying the body, the Brahmanical sacred thread is temporarily set aside
errors.why: The Tibetan says the brahmanical thread, since it merely purifies the body, is set aside; the English makes purifying the body the means of setting it aside.
rin po che'i tshogs is 'collection/mass of jewels' (ratna-gaṇa/-rāśi), not ratnamālā (which would be phreng ba); the note presents an unsupported Sanskrit title as the original.

note: Good reading of the Heruka etymology, the five mudrās and the three purities; the opening clause and the colophon note are off.

errors.english: means that these three joys are, in their proper manner, the very essence of both cyclic existence and the state beyond suffering
errors.why: The Tibetan gives a reason (phyir): the innate is neither existence nor nirvāṇa because those three joys are of the nature of existence and nirvāṇa; dropping 'because' makes 'neither' appear to mean that they are both.

note: Accurate treatment of the joys, the initiations and the lalanā/rasanā glosses; one explanatory sentence loses its causal link.
Faithful rendering of Yaśomitra's discussion of the results of śaikṣa/aśaikṣa and the 'in order' (yathākramam) principle.
